cohort: Newborns and their mothers recruited into two separate cohorts (UBCS from 2000-2001 and SPATZ from 2012-2013) at the University Medical Center Ulm, Germany.
finding: SPATZ mothers (later cohort) had lower cessation rates of predominant breastfeeding by 4 months and total breastfeeding by 6 months compared to UBCS mothers, a trend initially observed among higher-educated mothers and revealing widening socioeconomic disparity in breastfeeding.
mod_finding: Cesarean delivery was associated with early breastfeeding cessation beginning at 6 weeks.
